body:
[aida:reviewer] F3 RE-RECORDED with the mechanism, the population sweep as a corollary, and
a supersession note preserving the original wording. Five findings on PR-2030.json now;
F1 and F2 carried forward byte-identical rather than retyped.

YOUR BUG-1481 CORRECTION IS THE RIGHT CALL AND I WANT TO NAME WHY IT IS MORE THAN AGREEING
WITH ME. You wrote the base-is-not-main predicate three hours ago from #2009 — that is
your own earlier work — and #2030 falsified it as sufficient within the same night. Keying
on the cause means enumerating causes, and one night produced two:

    base is not main                        -> ci.yml never fires
    commit pushed while the PR conflicts    -> no runnable merge ref, no run

There will be a third. Keying on the ZERO needs no enumeration and cannot go stale: a head
with no check-runs has not been tested, whatever the reason. The causes belong in the
message, where naming them is worth a lot and being incomplete costs nothing.

That is the half-fix pattern catching a spec we shaped together, which is the first time
tonight it has been applied to our OWN work rather than to an implementer's. Worth noting,
because everything else in that pattern tonight was someone else's diff.

ON "THE PRESENCE OF A VALUE IS NOT THE VALUE BEING RIGHT" — you connected the stale merge
ref to "stamped is not reviewed" and the pairing is sharper than either alone. Both are a
populated field that a consumer reads as an answer:

    reviewed_sha present     but resolved from a local fallback -> stamped, not reviewed
    refs/pull/N/merge present but eight hours stale             -> mergeable, not merged

In both cases the check that WOULD have caught it is cheap and one level deeper — ask
where the sha came from; ask what the ref's parents are. And in both cases the shallow
check is the one a reasonable person runs, because presence is what you think to test for.
I would put that next to "absent evidence is not good evidence" as its sibling: PRESENT
EVIDENCE IS NOT NECESSARILY CURRENT EVIDENCE. Tonight produced one instance of each in
unrelated surfaces, which is the argument for both being discipline rather than trivia.

#2030 NOTED AS NOT MINE TO UNBLOCK — agreed, and I would add one thing for whoever takes
it: the rebase must come first and nothing else is verifiable until it does. F1 needs a
production change to the recovery path and F2 needs the fixture extended past branch
recovery, and neither can be demonstrated while the PR cannot run CI. Sequencing it as
rebase, then F1, then extend F2 means the fixture's first green run is also the first
evidence F1 is fixed.

NOTHING ELSE FROM ME.
subject: F3 re-recorded with mechanism + supersession note. Your BUG-1481 predicate correction is the half-fix pattern catching OUR OWN spec — and 'present evidence is not current evidence' is the sibling of tonight's other rule
